description: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "L" so every layer uses full-context attention.
Randomly replace 2% of input tokens with random vocab tokens during training (targets unchanged) as data-noise regularization.
Lower UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.0001 so the lm_head updates very slowly.
Add 5% LR warmup, creep LR slowly from 1.0 to 0.7 over the middle of training, then drop sharply to 0 over the last 20%.
Replace the static SSSL window pattern with a window that grows geometrically with depth (256,256,512,512,1024,1024,2048,2048 for 8 layers), since FA3 cannot take a true per-token window.
No change: the idea doesn't map onto this train.py.
Add a constant 1e-4 sign-of-momentum increment to the AdamW update so there is a baseline push in the update direction even when the Adam term decays.

issues: Measurement integrity: the diff only adds training-time input-token noise. With probability 0.005, each input token is swapped for a random token id, and the targets y stay the same. It does not touch the evaluation call, the data loading, the seed lines or the val_bpb computation, and the harness reported no integrity flags.

Possible bug, checked and ruled out: the code relies on `vocab_size` being defined in train.py's scope. The run finished and produced a value, so the name resolved. Random ids from randint_like(x, vocab_size) stay within the embedding range, so the result is valid.

Side effect: the extra torch.rand and randint calls use up RNG state, which changes the random stream later in the run. The seed lines themselves are unchanged, so this is allowed, but it makes comparisons against the incumbent's per-step randomness noisier.

Can't recompute z: the incumbent's standard deviation isn't given. The difference is 1.1146 - 1.1144 = 0.0002 lower for the candidate. For z = 0.026 to hold, the denominator has to be about 0.0077, which seems large for run-to-run noise at this scale and is worth checking. Even so, a gain of 0.0002 from a single run is far too small to count as a real improvement, so 'reject' is the right call however z is computed.
Only one candidate run was made, so the evidence is weak. There is no clear reason to spend a replicate slot on a change whose effect is near zero.

description: Randomly replace 0.5% of input tokens with random vocab tokens during training (targets unchanged).
Store AdamW exp_avg and exp_avg_sq in bf16 while doing the update math in fp32.
Warm up LR over the first 10% of training for the lm_head, token embedding and value embedding groups only, while Muon matrix and scalar groups run at full LR from step 0.

Compute the training loss only on even-index target positions on even steps and odd-index positions on odd steps (other targets set to ignore_index), so lm_head gets gradients from alternating position parities.
During the first half of training, zero the gradients of odd-indexed transformer blocks on every other step, so those layers are only updated every second step (semi-frozen).
No change: the Adam update already runs only on CUDA, and no mixed-device partial-sum logic exists in train.py.
Quantize the schedule progress into 50 discrete waves so LR multiplier and weight decay stay constant within each wave (staircase schedule).
Set WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.3 so the LR ramps up linearly over the first 30% of the time budget (the spec's DANSE setting has no counterpart in train.py, so it is skipped).
Add gradient-norm clipping at 0.1 (none existed) just before the optimizer step.
Add gradient-norm clipping at 0.1 (none existed) just before the optimizer step.
Accumulate gradients for the AdamW param groups over 10 steps and apply one Adam update with the averaged gradient at the end of each window (Muon unchanged).
Set DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE from 64 to 4 so each optimizer step uses 64 small micro-batches (same total batch size) instead of 8.
Comment out the RMS norm applied to token embeddings right after the wte lookup, so embedding magnitudes are no longer normalized.
Raise MATRIX_LR to 0.05 and make the LR decay linearly from 1.0 to 0.6 over the first half of training, then warm down linearly to zero over the second half.
Shrink the rotary cos/sin cache from 10x to 1x the sequence length, since only the first sequence_len positions are ever used.
